Kuvitus: ydinvoimala kallioisella merenr: Illustration: a nuclear power plant on a rocky sea shore. In the middle is a cylindrical reactor building with part of its dome drawn open: inside, the reactor core glows in the water. Next to it is a long turbine hall and behind it are the pylons of a power line. In front is the sea and in the sky a few clouds.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: ytimen sidosenerg: Graph to scale: the binding energy per nucleon of a nucleus in megaelectronvolts as a function of the mass number, from zero to 240. The points have been calculated from atomic masses: deuterium 1.1, helium-4 7.1, carbon-12 7.7, iron-56 8.8, krypton-92 8.5, barium-141 8.3 and uranium-235 7.6 megaelectronvolts. The curve rises steeply for light nuclei, is highest at iron and falls gently towards heavy nuclei. On the left, an arrow from the light nuclei obliquely up and to the right towards the peak: fusion. On the right, an arrow from uranium obliquely up and to the left to the medium-heavy nuclei: fission.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: uraani-235:: Schematic figure, not to scale: the fission of uranium-235 in three steps from left to right. A slow neutron hits a uranium-235 nucleus. A uranium-236 nucleus forms, which vibrates and stretches until it pinches. The nucleus splits into two medium-heavy nuclei, barium and krypton, which fly off at high speed in different directions, and three new neutrons are released at the same time.
Kaavakuva kolmesta ketjureaktiosta, kolm: Schematic figure of three chain reactions, three generations from top to bottom. On the left the multiplication factor k is 0.5: the generations have 4, 2 and 1 neutrons, so the chain dies out. In the middle k is 1: every generation has 2 neutrons, so the chain stays steady. On the right k is 2: there are 1, 2 and 4 neutrons, so the chain grows. The neutrons are grey dots.
Kaavakuva, ei mittakaavassa: deuteriumin: Schematic figure, not to scale: the fusion of deuterium and tritium. On the left, a deuterium nucleus with one proton and one neutron and a tritium nucleus with one proton and two neutrons approach each other at high speed, although their positive charges repel each other. On the right, a helium-4 nucleus and a free neutron have formed from them, and an energy of 17.6 megaelectronvolts is released.
Periaatekuva, ei mittakaavassa: vaaka, j: Schematic figure, not to scale: a balance with a uranium-235 nucleus and a neutron in the left pan, 236.0526 atomic mass units in total, and the products of the reaction, barium-141, krypton-92 and three neutrons, in the right pan, 235.8666 atomic mass units in total. The left side is heavier. The mass difference of 0.1860 atomic mass units is released as the energy Q, about 173 megaelectronvolts.
Periaatekuva painevesireaktorilla toimiv: Schematic figure of a nuclear power plant with a pressurised-water reactor, not to scale. On the left is the pressure vessel of the reactor: in the water there are fuel rods, and between them control rods lowered from above. The hot water circulates to the steam generator, where the water of the second circuit boils into steam. The steam turns a turbine, which turns a generator. The steam coming from the turbine condenses back into water in the condenser, which is cooled by sea water.
Periaatekuva Olkiluodon loppusijoituslai: Schematic figure of Onkalo, the final disposal facility at Olkiluoto, the depth scale to scale, the canister enlarged. On the left is the ground surface and below it the bedrock, through which an access tunnel runs to a depth of about 430 metres. Deep in the rock is a horizontal disposal tunnel, with canisters in holes drilled in its floor. On the right is an enlargement: the spent fuel is inside a cast-iron insert, around it is a copper canister, and around the canister is bentonite clay in the rock hole.
Kuvaaja mittakaavassa: ytimen sidosenerg: Graph to scale: the binding energy per nucleon of a nucleus in megaelectronvolts as a function of the mass number, mass number from 20 to 240, vertical axis from 7.0 to 9.0. The grid spacing is 10 horizontally and 0.1 megaelectronvolts vertically. The curve is highest at about mass number 60 and falls gently towards heavy nuclei. The vertical axis has a break mark because the axis does not start from zero.
